Terrace escarpments, loamy (TCb).
This is a miscellaneous land type that is on the steep, eroded edges of fans, terraces, and footslopes in river and intermittent stream valleys. The areas are 100 to 500 feet wide and usually separate soils on the main body of the fans and terraces from those that occupy the floodplains along the valley floor. In places where the valley bottoms are narrow, they were included with this land type in mapping. Erosion is active on this land type. Slopes are short and uneven. Local relief is 15 to 30 feet. Slopes range from 8 to 50 percent with 5 to 25 percent being average. Texture of the material ranges from clay loam to fine sandy loam. Stratification is common.
The surface runoff is rapid, and the erosion hazard is severe.
This land type is suited to range.
(Capability Unit VIe Dryland; Thin Hilly range site 10-14 inch precipitation zone; Windbreak Suitability Group 4)
